'''Dr. Rajat Subhra Hazra''' is an Indian mathematician specialising in [[probability theory]]. He was awarded the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], the highest science award in India, for the year 2020 in mathematical science category.<ref>{{cite news |title=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize 2020: Pathbreaking research that won 14 scientists India's top science prize |url=https://www.firstpost.com/tech/science/shanti-swarup-bhatnagar-prize-2020-meet-the-14-scientists-engineers-who-bagged-indias-top-science-prize-8858261.html |work=Tech2 |publisher=Firstpost |date=29 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=SSB awardee in 2020|url=https://ssbprize.gov.in/WriteReadData/LatestUpdates/202009260117197601874ShantiSwarupBhatnagarPrize2020Website.pdf|website=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize|publisher=CSIR Human Resource Development Group, New Delhi}}</ref> He is affiliated to the Mathematical Institute of Leiden University, the Netherlands from 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/staffmembers/rajat-hazra#tab-1 | title=Rajat Hazra }}</ref> Prior to that he was affiliated to Indian Statistical Institute, Kolkata. Dr. Hazra has a very broad range of research interests including extreme value theory, regular variation, random matrices, free probability, Gaussian free fields, branching random walks, membrane models, random graphs, etc.<ref>{{cite web |title=Indian Statistical Institute - Faculty profiles |url=https://isi.irins.org/profile/111487 |website=irins.inflibnet.ac.in |publisher=[[INFLIBNET Centre]] |language=en}}</ref>

He is well known for his out of the box analysis of day to day events. A recent example came into limelight when he asked an exam question with  ''Covfefe'', a word that featured in US President Donald Trump’s tweet for random sequence of letters.<ref>{{cite news |title=ISI Kolkata professor gives the answer to the viral Donald Trump 'COVFEFE' question |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/trending/trending-in-india/answer-to-donald-trumps-covfefe-question-at-isi-kolkata-4967285/ |work=The Indian Express |date=4 December 2017 |language=en}}</ref>

He is an elected Fellow of [[Indian Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Rajat Subhra Hazra - Fellow profile |url=https://fellows.ias.ac.in/profile/v/FL2020023 |website=fellows.ias.ac.in |publisher=[[Indian Academy of Sciences]] |accessdate=22 October 2020}}</ref>
